payload.pattern: A PostgreSQL IMMUTABLE partial-index expression can silently abort the entire transactional migration, rolling back unrelated statements while a higher-level runner appears to continue.
payload.solution: Preflight expression volatility, isolate risky index DDL, and verify both schema effects and the migration-ledger row before promotion; never infer success from runner continuation alone.

payload.pattern: An artifact that NAMES an owner but resolves its destination from process.cwd() can land in the wrong repo, and a completion gate that matches such artifacts by filename alone will accept a foreign one as its own evidence.
payload.evidence: studio-ops S309 found six repo: atlas closeout briefs inside studio-ops/docs (four committed). render-closeout-brief.mjs archived to join(process.cwd(), docs) while the payload carried repo, and check-closeout-session-coherence.mjs derived its closeoutBrief surface from the max filename session number with no ownership filter. A sibling at an equal-or-higher session number would have satisfied studio-ops closeout gate with a brief studio-ops never rendered.
payload.solution: Bind the artifact to the identity it claims. scripts/lib/artifact-ownership.mjs is a pure helper: repoIdentity() builds the alias set a repo answers to (registry slug + directory name + remote repo name), classifyOwnership() returns owned/foreign/unmarked, extractBriefRepoClaim() reads the declared owner. Writers refuse a mismatch out loud with a named opt-out; consumers filter by owner and REPORT the foreign ones rather than swallowing them.
payload.criticalDetail: Treat unmarked (no owner claim) as OWNED, not foreign. Legacy artifacts predate the owner field, and dropping them would trade a false green for a false red — the same lie pointed the other way.
payload.generalization: This is the same root as the propagated-script trap where a tool resolves its root from import.meta.dirname and silently measures the control plane instead of you: whenever a tool derives WHERE from one source and WHAT from another, make it compare the two and say so.

payload.context: StatVault S291. S290 shipped two profile panels, verified them against production by fetching ONE url, found no heading, and filed a blocking finding naming the loader as the suspect with box SSH as the next step. The page is served as THREE chapters behind a ?chapter= query param; the default chapter deliberately carries no stat tables. The panels had been rendering the whole time. Same commit, no code change: default 0/0/0, ?chapter=story 1/2/47 (panel A / panel B / <table>).
payload.solution: Before concluding 'X does not render in production', establish the SET of served surfaces and read all of it. Two traps make the wrong conclusion feel well-evidenced: (1) every individual exclusion can be CORRECT, so eliminating real causes narrows toward a cause that does not exist; (2) the corroborating marker you pick to prove you are on the right code path may itself live on the surface you already fetched, so it cannot discriminate. The durable fix is to DECLARE the surface set in one artifact the UI renders from, then have the live probe enumerate it rather than sample it. Two design notes that matter: grade HEADINGS not page text (a nav prints every surface's label on every surface, so substring matching makes 'absent elsewhere' unfalsifiable), and WITHHOLD rather than redden while production lags the tree that declares the contract — otherwise the gate is red for the length of every deploy window, which is an unsatisfiable assertion, not a high standard.

payload.context: StatVault S291, closing a commitment that read 'the corpus is correct and nothing regenerates it — wire the ingests into the nightly refresh lane'. Doing exactly that would have changed nothing: both ingests hard-coded their upper season bound to a literal year, so a nightly lane would have re-fetched the same nine seasons forever while every freshness surface reported a healthy pipeline feeding a frozen corpus.
payload.solution: A staleness budget measured in DAYS cannot see a bound measured in SEASONS (or versions, or regions, or tenants). When closing a freshness item, check the producer's RANGE as well as its cadence, and derive the range rather than pinning it. Then grade currency against what the SOURCE actually publishes, never against the calendar: here the upstream release held 1,822 assets and none for the season the calendar named, so a calendar rule would have been permanently unclearable. Have the producer RECORD what the source had (a provenance artifact) and let the gate compare artifact-vs-source, disclosing the calendar gap instead of failing on it. Related: the ingest already printed '(skip 2025: HTTP 404)' and exited 0 — an absence that appears only in stdout is not recorded, and downstream it reads as a clean success that happened to produce less data.

payload.headline: Model pins are floating aliases; model currency is an expiring attestation, not an assertion.
patterns: A fallback that is also a legitimate answer is invisible: when could-not-determine and the-answer-is-X produce identical output, every failed lookup reads as a decision.
A dated model ID decays silently. Guard pins with an allowlist of floating aliases, never a denylist of known-bad IDs, which goes stale exactly like the thing it guards.
A rule branch that matches zero rows is dead code wearing the costume of policy. Make unevaluable predicates throw.
Fix the chokepoint, not the visible copy: check which copy actually executes before claiming coverage.
A propagator must be able to write to its own repo; a lock belonging to THIS session is why the write is safe.

payload.headline: The deploy gate asked the readiness endpoint a liveness question, for eight releases

patterns.name: ask-the-endpoint-that-owns-the-question
patterns.lesson: When a check is answering the wrong question, look FIRST for the surface that already answers the right one. VEILOS' deploy gate asserted status===200 on /_health while /health/live answered liveness unconditionally one route above and had never been called. Third consecutive session where the correct remedy was already in the tree and merely unlinked.
patterns.applies_to: any repo whose health/readiness endpoints are distinct but whose CI asserts 200 on one of them

patterns.name: verdict-vocabulary-must-match-its-subject
patterns.lesson: A gate recording pass/fail cannot express a state that is true, known and deliberately chosen. VEILOS' founder ruled that production report ready:false over a real storage breach; the gate then went red on every deploy for a CORRECT state. A gate that reds on the state the founder chose is a gate that gets waved through, and a waved-through gate can no longer report a real outage. Add a third member, give it its own glyph and its own column, and let only failures move the exit code.
patterns.applies_to: any release gate, smoke runner, or CI check with a boolean verdict over a three-state subject

patterns.name: an-instrument-is-only-tested-once-it-has-met-a-second-world
patterns.lesson: Twelve unit tests with hand-built fixtures passed a row that attributed EVERY not-ready state to one specific founder ruling. It was false the first time it met a staging isolate, because every fixture the author wrote carried the production shape. Deploy to staging BEFORE trusting a green suite about anything environment-shaped.
patterns.applies_to: any project with a staging environment and environment-conditional assertions

patterns.name: a-declared-denominator-is-an-exception-list-until-checked
patterns.lesson: VEILOS' DEPLOYABLE_PATHS manifest names three scripts and none of their 24 transitive dependencies, two of which author the runtime bindings the deploy stamps into the Worker. Hand-maintained since S252, never once checked against the world. Walk the import closure of any hand-maintained manifest and publish the gap as a ceiling that may only shrink.
patterns.applies_to: any repo with a hand-maintained list answering 'did anything deployable change?'

patterns.name: witness-alignment-is-a-fixpoint-not-an-ordering
patterns.lesson: Three receipts (test, doctor, readiness) must all bind to one tree hash before deploy. Receipts are excluded from the hash; the status JSON is not, and both the doctor and the readiness writer touch it. Re-ordering steps does not solve this - run each writer twice until the hash stops moving, THEN take the suite witness. Cost four full suite runs to learn.
patterns.applies_to: any repo gating deploys on tree-bound test/doctor receipts

payload.honesty: Six of this repository's own instruments refused this session's work and all six were right, including one enforcing a lesson already written in the agent's memory. Two founder-owned promises were renewed rather than decided, one with its renewal premise corrected because its own authority had refuted it. The residual breach is REPORTED and not REMEDIED, growing across three sessions: 158,872 -> 170,924 -> 173,155 B.

payload.context: StatVault S291. A gate had reported for three sessions that 'the box is not running this repository's data-refresh.sh', and its own message said to ESCALATE TO THE BOX rather than re-derive from committed evidence, 'which has now twice been insufficient'. Two sessions re-read the same receipt and deferred. The SSH credential was READY the whole time. One command answered it: the control repo the box's systemd units execute from was 123 commits and 11 days behind origin/main, on a clean checkout with no local commits.
payload.solution: A release lane that fetches origin/main and builds every release in a DETACHED WORKTREE never advances the control repo's own working tree. Anything rooted there — cron units, timers, watchdogs, refresh jobs — silently runs whatever it was last checked out at, and no repo-side surface can see the drift. The sharpest consequence is that a fix which lands on main may never execute: S291 wired two ingests into the nightly refresh, and the box's copy of that file predated the change by 11 days. Fix: fast-forward the control repo after a GREEN promotion (the moment the commit is proven by CI, staging and a live smoke), with --ff-only so a local commit the lane did not push REFUSES loudly instead of being discarded, placed after the deploy receipt so a refusal cannot roll back a good deploy. Two further notes: this only fires when a release SUCCEEDS, so a long-red lane re-freezes the checkout and deserves its own freshness receipt; and when a gate tells you to go look at the machine, the machine is where the answer is — re-deriving from committed evidence is what it already told you is insufficient.

payload.headline: S279 finalized: Agent Studio flagship + passkey re-sign-in fix + edit surfaces, PLUS two post-ship review cycles that caught (1) a live open redirect the re-sign-in fix itself introduced and (2) two of that batch fixes regressing. All fixed, staging-verified, deployed 82de8e7a.
payload.lesson: Run /code-review over your OWN diff after done, and again over the fix commits; a control a fix introduces is a control an attacker targets; when a gate refuses your score, lower the score not the gate (sil-evidence-ceiling caught automationCoverage 97 > ceiling 85, lowered to 85).

payload.topWin: the audit found nine defects and then found that five of them were one defect. The remedy-drift gate exists because this repo's failure mode has stopped being blindness and become inaction — 185 detection probes and, until now, nothing that made a standing detection expire.

payload.headline: Big sprint — shipped 10 substantive changes, headlined by remedy-drift gate.
bullets: **Remedy-drift gate** — standing detections can now expire; the class fix for five of nine findings.
**Audit-premise checker** — permanently UNMEASURED to 3.0s, with verdict parity proven.
**Rolling-status header** — re-derived, and the closeout now asserts the outcome instead of assuming it.
**Blocker cascade** — `unknown` removed from the ranking, coverage published, artifact 28 days fresher.
**Genius de-phantom** — reads the board's tag-reference closures; completed work no longer ranks CRITICAL.
**Unmapped-warnings gate** — three-state; a stale snapshot is UNVERIFIED, never a pass or a fail.
**Frontier source contract** — a declared floor plus required IDs, replacing a literal that broke on a correct change.
**Runway signal** — three-state grading, and the field now carries a real measure.
**Two printed remedies run** — promogrind baton shipped (17/17), deploy gaps measured (5/8 SPARKED flagged).
**Second-order** — SCORE-table decomposition parser (2/17 to 17/17), `drift` allowlisted as a family word, and a model-literal assertion replaced by its invariant.
